issues.title: [Bug]: annotation on a local variable declaration crashes the compiler (INTERNAL_ERROR: expression type not resolved for *ast.BLangLiteral)
issues.output:
valid variant:
fatal[INTERNAL_ERROR]: expression type not resolved
 --> i1423.bal:6:5

invalid variant (annotation x on type; @x on local var):
fatal[INTERNAL_ERROR]: expression type not resolved
 --> i1423b.bal:6:5
(the same annotation on a module-level var correctly reports: error[SEMANTIC_ERROR]: annotation 'x' is not allowed on var)
issues.reasoning: Reproduces on main (message text now lacks the '*ast.BLangLiteral' suffix). Spec 2024R1 §7.11 allows [annots] on local-init-var-decl-stmt and §9.1 lists local-var-decl-stmt under the source-only 'var' attach point, so the first program must compile and print 2; the second must give a normal attach-point diagnostic. Clean-context spec check agreed. The front end fails during type resolution of the annotation on a local var decl and cannot produce BIR -> frontend. Not frontend-crash: it is an INTERNAL_ERROR diagnostic, not a Go panic. No duplicate found among existing issues (related annotation issues #1335, #1239 cover other attach points).

issues.title: [Bug]: rest parameter list is created read-only (push/assignment panics with "cannot mutate readonly value")
issues.output:
true
error: inherent type violation: cannot mutate readonly value
        at setFirst(i1424.bal:9)
           main(i1424.bal:19)
issues.reasoning: Reproduces on main. Spec §7.3.1: the rest param is initialised to a newly created list whose inherent type is T[] (not readonly); 'implicitly final' only forbids reassigning the parameter variable. Clean-context spec check agreed. Root cause is in the interpreter: runtime/internal/exec/terminators.go:358 and runtime/internal/exec/executor.go:100 call values.NewList(..., true /*readonly*/, ...) for the rest list -> backend. No duplicate found; #471 (closed, rest-arg list type creation in runtime) is related but distinct.

issues.title: [Bug]: spreading a variable-length list into a tuple with a minimum length is not rejected (creates a list shorter than its inherent type)
issues.output:
compiles without error, then:
error: invalid array index: 0
        at main(i1425.bal:6)
issues.reasoning: Reproduces on main. Spec §6.7.1: if a spread member's type is not fixed length, the minimum number of members it and previous members may add must be >= the inherent type's minimum length; int[] contributes min 0 but [int, int...] needs 1, so a compile-time error is required. Clean-context spec check agreed. Missing semantic check, so the front end emits BIR for an invalid program -> frontend (no crash). No duplicate; #1109 (open) is the opposite case (fixed-length spread wrongly rejected) in the same list-constructor spread check and could be fixed together.
